_squads: Bot squads in duos and trios (brmatch.ts). Ours, after every battle royale's squads: a squad follows its first bot, the others keeping spread metres apart around it and closing in when further than follow metres; a bot that sees someone tells its mates within share metres, who go to look; a downed target counts downedFar times as far off, so a bot turns to whoever is still up. A squad's bot knocked while a mate stands is down, not out (src/config/squad.json's bleed-out, crawl and revive, as a player's): a mate with nothing in sight within reviveRange m walks over and picks it up. crouchWalk is a crouched bot's share of its tier's speed, which the crawl is a share of in turn. The traversal (brmatch.ts botTraversal): a bot within ropeReach m of a zipline's end, standing on the floor under it, takes the rope when its far end is at least rideGain m nearer where the bot is going; a launch pad throws any bot that steps on it, as it throws a player. How a bot squad holds together and takes the map's ways across it: follow is how far a follower may be thrown from its lead, ropeReach how near a rope's end it has to stand, rideGain how much nearer the far end has to be, and towerGain how far its goal has to be before it rides a jump tower (a balloon costs it the climb and the fall, so it is only worth it for a long way).
_note: Bot difficulty tiers (src/game/bots.ts). The shape follows how Counter-Strike 2's shipped bot profile and Valve's published Team Fortress 2 bot code grade their bots (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_12.md section 4): a reaction time to a newly seen enemy, an aim that re-settles on an interval (here, how far behind a moving target the aim lags), a starting aim error that shrinks while it keeps the target (errStart degrees, errDecay = the fraction of the extra error left after one second, errFloor what it settles to), where on the body it aims (height in m above the feet), the chance to dodge when shot, the chance to hear a shot within earshot, grenades, cover and a crouch while firing. Reaction and the error's start and decay are CS2's values where its tiers line up (Easy, Normal, Hard, Expert); the rest are ours, tuned so each tier plays differently rather than only aiming differently.
_mixed: a battle royale's 'mixed' lobby: each bot's tier drawn with these weights
_grenade: a bot's frags: how many it carries, the least time between two, the range it throws over (m), and how long a target must have stood still in view (grenadeAfter, per tier) or been out of sight behind cover (hiddenAfter) before it throws at where it was
_cover: a bot with cover on, hurt below this fraction of its shield and health, looks for a spot within these metres out of the target's sight to heal, then peeks back
_hearing: a shot within this many metres can be heard (by the tier's chance): the bot turns and goes to look, for this many seconds
_dodge: hurt, a bot that dodges reverses its strafe and strafes harder for this long
_sight: How far a bot can see someone, metres (bots.ts sees()). 60 m was right for the arena, which is 36 m by 64, and blind on the battle royale's 440 m map, whose defining feature is 100 to 165 m of open ground between places, so the range is per mode and per tier: an arena bot still fights at arena range, while a battle royale elite holds a ridge and an easy one has to come down off it. What the target is doing counts, because spotting is about how much of it there is to see: a body at a run is picked up further out (`moving`, full value at `at` m/s), a crouched one behind cover much later, and a muzzle flash gives a shooter away at any range. `size` is the target's height against a standing body, scaled by `sizeGain`. Under `min` metres a bot always sees (someone in its face), over `max` it never does. A long gun sees `scoped` further and holds its angle at `holdFrac` of that range instead of walking into it: a long gun is one that still does its full damage past `longFrom` metres (the marksman and sniper family, whose falloff in the weapon data starts at 190 m where an SMG is done by 25) or one wearing a ranged optic it looted (the `scopes` prefixes). `far` keeps a long shot missable without a second model: the aim error is multiplied by 1 plus `perMetre` for every metre past `from`, so an elite bot spots you at 170 m and still has to work for the hit.

sight._cone: Ours, after every shooter's AI: a bot not in a fight sees only within cone degrees of the way it faces (past min metres; closer than that it always notices you). One that has seen someone in the last fightMemory seconds is looking round and sees all the way round. Bots used to see behind themselves, so a player could never come up on one unseen.
sight._recheck: Seconds a battle royale bot keeps what one line of sight told it before casting it again (brmatch.ts sense). The ray is the dear half of seeing; thirty in the city cast it at everyone in range every frame, 0.74 ms of a 6.5 ms frame (tools/profile-frame.ts). 0.1 s is under the quickest tier's reaction (0.12 s), so no bot notices sooner or later than it would have; each bot's checks fall on its own moments, so the work is spread over the frames.

_loot: A bot that lands with nothing loots like a player instead of waiting out a timer: it walks to the nearest thing on the floor it would rather have, inside `search` metres, and takes it once it is within `reach` and has spent `perItem` of its tier's botSearch (src/config/loot.json) rummaging, so an easy bot fumbles over every item and an elite one is quick. It looks again every `rescan` seconds, gives a spot up after `giveUp` seconds of not getting there (a wall in the way), stops after `window` of those botSearches or once its kit scores `enough`, and scores its kit by `score`, where a gun is worth most and armour next. There are no body shields on this map's floor (a player's shield EVOs instead), so kitting up stands in for them: every `armorPerItems` things it takes is worth a tier of shield up to `maxArmor`, and a helmet is worth the tier in `helmetTier` at once (those match the helmet armour in items.json to the dummy's shield tiers). That is what makes a bot that landed in a rich place better armed than one that landed in a field.

loot._overtime: how many of its own search windows a bot that still has NO gun may spend before it gives up and fights unarmed. The window alone used to end the search, so a bot that landed badly stopped looking and stayed unarmed, held its fire for the whole match and walked the ring as a free kill. Ours.
loot._floor: how far above or below its feet, in metres, an item may be for a bot to go for it. A bot cannot jump or climb, so an item on the floor above can be a metre away across the ground and out of reach for ever: in a probe, one stood under loot on an upper floor for the whole 40 s, unarmed. A storey here is 3.4 m, so 1.2 keeps a bot to its own floor with room for a crate top. Ours.

_arc: grenade.arcSlack and arcTries: before a bot throws, it traces its lob against the world. The first arc it tries is the flight the throw has always used; if that would strike something more than arcSlack metres short of where it is aiming (a roof, a wall, the building over the circle), it tries the steeper lobs in arcTries, and if none lands within arcSlack across and arcRise up or down it keeps the frag for later: a frag on the roof right over your head is close across and a floor away. A probe of the tiers test caught an elite bot's frag going off 14 m from its target one run in two, into whatever stood in the arc's way. Ours.
_beginner: SpeedKills' fifth tier, below easy (plan section 7.12, the owner's five): walks rather than strafes, reacts in 0.9 s, misses wide and settles loose, fires a third as often, and takes cover when hurt, so a new player can learn to fight one. Ours.
_skHacks: SpeedKills: the hacks a bot carries by its tier, and when it uses them (bots.ts stepSk). Heal (hacks.json heal: health back over its seconds) once its health and shield are under healBelow of full; Dash (hacks.json dash: its distance over its seconds, across the line of fire, stopped by walls) when hit within dashWhenHitWithin seconds with a target in view. Cooldowns are the hacks' own at fusion level 0. A beginner uses none, so it can be learned on. Ours.
_maxStep: Metres: the longest single step a bot's walk is made of in one go (bots.ts). A frame's walk longer than this (a slow frame: dt runs to 0.1 s, and 0.1 s at 6.6 m/s is 0.66 m) is walked in pieces, each with its own wall check and slide, as a quick frame would have walked it. 0.2 m is a quick frame's step at the fastest tier's pace and 30 fps.
